hero.title: Hormuz, tariffs, 5% rates.
hero.title_em: The world’s crises now ship with every parcel.
hero.dek: Fuel, air freight, the end of duty exemptions, network consolidation: how global tensions travel, link by link, into the cost and speed of a parcel.

chain.t: Hormuz: war since February, strait restricted, Brent above $100
US–China truce: tariff cuts on ~$30bn each way
US and EU: small-parcel duty exemption ends
Local stock, network consolidation, landed price guaranteed at checkout

wire.text: of InPost shareholders tender their shares to the Advent, FedEx, A&R and PPF consortium. The 80% threshold is cleared: Europe’s parcel-locker leader changes hands.
Temu is now level with Amazon in cross-border purchases, up from under 1% in 2022.

wire.lede: 61% say knowing delivery and customs charges before buying is “essential”.
J&T Express now earns half its revenue outside China; H1 profit doubled.

wire.text: parcel points for Royal Mail after IDS agreed to buy an open UK network of about 3,000 lockers, due to complete by the end of 2026.

wire.lede: Canada Post raises its peak out-of-spec surcharge from C$300 to C$400 per item from 2 November to 10 January.
Estafeta puts MXN193m into its State of Mexico operations and more than 1,500 jobs; Geodis adds MXN100m in Tultepec.
Coupang's Rocket Delivery now reaches about 70% of Taiwan, seven days a week, for more than 10,000 Korean sellers.

why.title: Hormuz puts a fuel bill on every air parcel
why.what: Brent has been above $100 since the war began in February.
why.why: Integrators and Asia–Europe air freight pass it on through fuel surcharges.
why.means: Cross-border margins are squeezed just before peak season.

why.title: The $800 free pass is gone. US clearance now runs on data
why.what: The de minimis exemption has been suspended indefinitely since 24 June 2026.
why.why: Duties are now paid monthly by a designated filer, usually the operator.
why.means: An edge for those who master customs data: classification, origin, value.

why.title: A trade truce, but no return to direct small parcels
why.what: Tariff cuts on about $30bn of goods each way in September.
why.why: The US de minimis exemption is not restored by the truce.
why.means: Platforms keep moving stock into local warehouses.

deals.deal: New parcel distribution centre in Maldegem (7,930 m²)
Raised TIM offer: €6.65 a share, two-thirds threshold dropped

global_coming.what: US midterm elections, with tariffs a key voter issue.

emea.title: Europe taxes the parcel.
emea.dek: From 1 November a low-value parcel into the EU pays a €3 duty per tariff line plus a €2 handling fee, the UK has set a date to close its £135 gap, Hormuz keeps Brent above $100, and North Africa's ports are becoming Europe's nearest gateway.

chain.t: €3 duty per tariff line since July, €2 handling fee per item from 1 November
£135 relief removed by October 2028; Autumn Budget on 28 October
Hormuz restricted and no ceasefire: Brent at $104 on 28 September
Tanger Med and Suez rerouting make North Africa Europe's nearest hub

apac.title: Asia-Pacific closes the duty-free door at different speeds.
apac.title_em: The parcel pays at checkout, at the pump and at the US border.
apac.dek: Japan moves the tax on small imports to the checkout from 2028, Korea makes foreign platforms answer locally, Southeast Asia writes one digital rulebook, India opens parcel exports, and Australia keeps its A$1,000 threshold.

chain.t: Japan taxes imports of ¥10,000 or less at checkout from April 2028
ASEAN digital economy agreement targeted for signature in Manila in November
India removed the courier export value cap; US entry filing now applies to every parcel
A$1,000 threshold kept, but fuel surcharges reached 19.5% at Australia Post
